listing_view.reasoning: Subscription built from ~1x midday on day 1 to ~71x by close, an accelerating pattern that signals strong demand and a likely oversubscribed listing pop. But this demand is momentum-driven and says nothing about fair value; at ₹403–424 no EPS/peer valuation is verifiable from what was given, so the pop could unwind fast.

longterm_view.reasoning: Revenue compounding near 40–47% is real, but it is being bought with a blade-thin EBITDA margin (~5.3%) and operating cash flow of only 26% of EBITDA, with OCF of ₹325m against ₹1,251m EBITDA in the latest year. Growth this fast in low-margin retail typically consumes working capital and debt (debt/equity 0.77, improving), so the quality of the growth is unproven.

governance.reasoning: A past SEBI monetary penalty of ₹2.5m is disclosed [litigation, page 544], though current litigation/disciplinary status is stated as clean [litigation, page 543]. Related-party disclosures exist but the extracts are too fragmentary to judge their substance.

key_risks.risk: Profit is not turning into cash
key_risks.why_it_matters: OCF is ₹325m vs EBITDA ₹1,251m (26% conversion) and was negative two years ago; if this persists, growth must be funded by debt or equity dilution.
At ~5.3% EBITDA margin, small cost or pricing shocks can erase profitability; the prospectus itself flags pricing pressure from e-commerce and local retailers.
A SEBI-imposed ₹2.5m penalty exists in the record, so the 'clean' litigation statement is only current as of the RHP date.
₹80m of performance bank guarantees are outstanding and revocation risk is expressly flagged as able to adversely affect the business.

answers.question: check receivables and inventory against the sales growth
answers.answer: Receivables support the growth: only 1.8–5.3 days of sales are outstanding across three years even as revenue grew 47% in the latest year, consistent with a cash-and-carry retail model rather than channel-stuffing. Inventory, however, cannot be checked — no inventory or inventory-days figure was given, and with OCF at only 26% of EBITDA, inventory build is the most likely place the cash went, so this check is only half done.

answer.what_would_change_my_mind: An inventory figure and cash-flow bridge showing where the ₹926m EBITDA-to-OCF gap went, plus any EPS or peer valuation data: if the gap is organic store build rather than receivable/inventory leakage, the longterm score rises materially.
